cards.text: David's son Absalom has turned against him (2 Samuel 15:10-12), and David has fled Jerusalem and crossed the Jordan River (2 Samuel 15:14; 17:22). Now David goes to a place called Mahanaim, and Absalom crosses the Jordan too, with all the men of Israel. Friend, when a father and son end up on opposite sides of a war, nobody's having a good week.
Absalom puts a man named Amasa over his army, in place of Joab, David's army commander (2 Samuel 8:16). And now the family tree gets TANGLED, friend.

cards.question: Amasa's mother Abigail is the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother. That makes Amasa and Joab ___.

cards.text: Absalom and the Israelites camp in the land of Gilead. When David reaches Mahanaim, three men come to meet him: Shobi from the Ammonite city of Rabbah, Machir from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite.

They bring beds, basins, clay pots, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, curds, sheep and cheese. Back when I lived in the Millers' kitchen, with the family who first took me home, a new neighbor got ONE batch of cookies from us and we felt like heroes.

cards.question: Shobi, Machir and Barzillai bring all of that for David and his people to eat. What reason do they give?

answers.text: The people are hungry and tired and thirsty
The king sent word asking for supplies
They want a place in the king's army

cards.text: Now David reviews his troops and appoints commanders over thousands and hundreds. He splits the army in three: one third under Joab, one under Joab's brother Abishai, and one under Ittai the Gittite, a foreigner loyal to David (2 Samuel 15:19-21).

cards.question: With his army split into three, what does King David tell the troops?

answers.text: He will march out with them
He will wait for more men
He will talk to Absalom first

cards.text: But his people plead, "You must not go out!" Picture telling your boss, "Respectfully, sir, please go sit in your office."

cards.question: Why don't David's people want the king out on the battlefield?

answers.text: He is worth ten thousand of them
Absalom's army is far too big
He has never led them in battle

cards.question: After his people plead with him, King David agrees to stay back from the battle.

cards.text: "I will do whatever seems best to you," David tells them. So the king stands beside the gate while the troops march out by hundreds and by thousands.

cards.question: King David has one order about his son for Joab, Abishai and Ittai. He commands them to treat the young man Absalom ___ for his sake.
Only Joab, Abishai and Ittai hear the king's order about Absalom.

cards.text: Here we go, friend. David's army marches into the field to face Israel.

cards.question: Where does the battle between David's army and Israel take place?
In the forest of Ephraim, the people of Israel, Absalom's side, are defeated by David's servants.

cards.text: The slaughter is great that day: twenty thousand men. The battle spreads over the whole countryside, and that day the forest devours more people than the sword.
Then Absalom, riding on his mule, runs into David's servants. The mule goes under the thick branches of a large oak.

cards.question: As his mule goes under those thick oak branches, Absalom's ___ gets caught fast in the tree.

cards.text: The mule under him keeps going like a coworker who walks off the second the boss asks who did this, and Absalom is left hanging in midair. One of David's men sees it and tells Joab, "I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree!"

cards.question: One of David's men sees Absalom hanging in the oak and tells Joab. How does Joab react?

answers.text: He asks why the man didn't strike him
He tells the man to go tell the king
He orders the man to cut him down

cards.question: Joab says he would have paid the man ten shekels of silver and a warrior's belt. The man tells Joab he would strike Absalom for a thousand shekels of silver.

cards.text: He won't raise his hand against the king's son. He reminds Joab they all heard the king command, 'Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.'

cards.question: The man believes that if he had killed Absalom, Joab would have stood by him.

cards.text: That man knows how it goes: do the risky thing, and the boss suddenly forgets your name. Then Joab says, "I am not going to wait like this with you!"

Joab takes three spears in his hand and thrusts them through the heart of Absalom while he is still alive in the oak tree. Then ten young men who carry Joab's armor surround Absalom, strike him and kill him.

cards.question: Then Joab blows the ram's horn. What do his troops do?

answers.text: March back to the king's gate

cards.question: What do Joab's men do with Absalom's body?

answers.text: Throw him in a pit under stones
Carry him back to King David
Bury him in his father's tomb

cards.question: Meanwhile, what do the Israelites who followed Absalom do?

answers.text: Flee each to his own home
Surrender to David at the gate

cards.text: Here's a sad little detail. During his lifetime, Absalom set up a pillar for himself in the King's Valley and gave it his own name.

cards.question: Absalom said he set up that pillar because he had no ___ to preserve the memory of his name.

cards.text: When this was written, it was still called Absalom's Monument. Don't hang up that apron yet, baker, because this story still has more to tell.
